plants.name: Tulipa gesneriana
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with cup-shaped flowers on sturdy stems above blue-green strap-like leaves. Late-season varieties are at peak bloom in early May across cool temperate gardens and commercial fields.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-spring (April to early May in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Netherlands, Northern Europe, northeastern United States, and temperate gardens worldwide; native to Central Asia
plants.funFact: During the Dutch 'Tulip Mania' of the 1630s, single bulbs sold for more than the price of a luxurious canal house.

plants.name: Syringa vulgaris
plants.description: A deciduous shrub producing dense, fragrant conical clusters of tiny four-lobed flowers. It reaches peak bloom in many northern temperate regions in early to mid May.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring (May in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Northern United States, Canada, Europe, and northern Asia; native to the Balkan Peninsula
plants.funFact: Lilac is in the olive family (Oleaceae), making it a relative of olive trees and jasmine.

plants.name: Wisteria sinensis
plants.description: A vigorous woody climbing vine that produces long, pendulous racemes of fragrant pea-like flowers, often before or as the leaves emerge. Blooms are still spectacular in early May in many regions.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late spring (April to May)
plants.location: Native to China; widely grown in Japan, Europe, and the southeastern and northeastern United States
plants.funFact: Wisteria vines can live for over a century, and some specimens in Japan are famous for flower trellises covering over 1,000 square meters.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A large evergreen shrub of the fynbos with enormous, bowl-shaped flower heads surrounded by showy bracts. In the Southern Hemisphere autumn, it begins to bloom in some areas, with peak season later in autumn and winter.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn to spring in South Africa (flowering can begin around May)
plants.location: Fynbos regions of the Western and Eastern Cape, South Africa
plants.funFact: The King Protea is South Africa's national flower, and the genus is named after the Greek god Proteus for its remarkable variety of forms.
